meta.notes: Revises a sentence when asked for a fact. Heard a drama line; composed "white hands". Rare finality sounds almost violent. Admission comes only if the player keeps asking.

threads.topic: "19 July." That's one of your notebooks.
Why is there a sill in your book?
threads.source: Suspect chain, the Prices. The accusation is the only proof either knows the other is there.

jp_p1.line: Don't touch "white." It took me an hour. "The set died at four minutes to nine and the wall went on talking, ticking as it talked, 'Inspector, the clock is four minutes fast,' and somebody slammed a door on it." And then white hands, museum-white, on the sill, or on a sill, or, no, it wants a sill.

jp_p1s.line: You've read it, then, and you're doing the silence critics do. It's very good. I've done it to Noel.

jp_p2.line: It wants two beats there. You can hear that.

jp_p3.line: No. The white was... it's a figure, it stands for... my brother's a conservator, it's a very rich... No.

jp_p4.line: The inspector's line. The door. The tick, I thought the tick was the play's clock. Through the wall, through her wall, when my set had gone. The hands are the sentence. I heard that. I didn't see anything. I have never in my life seen anything.

jp_f1.line: It has a beginning, which I've kept, and a second beginning. I wrote the neighbour an apology on Monday for the noise and by Thursday it was six pages and she owed me money.

jp_s1.line: It wants a sill. I don't know why it wants a sill. There's a draught under that door, it comes and goes, I've put it in four chapters.

choices.label: It comes when Noel comes. He tests it with his hand.

jp_s1s.line: You've got the look of someone with a better sentence. Everyone has one. Nobody brings it up the stairs.

jp_s2.line: He... cotton, I suppose, with the little tape. Every night? I gave those hands an hour. I thought it was a figure. Two flights, and he could knock. He won't, and I wouldn't answer. Don't put that anywhere.
